audit_findings_and_limitations.rul_cap_mismatch_resolved: The notebook trained with RUL capped at 130 cycles. The README claimed 125 cycles; this evaluation uses the true 130-cycle cap.
audit_findings_and_limitations.estimator_count_mismatch_resolved: The committed Random Forest model contains 200 estimators (not 100 as previously documented).
audit_findings_and_limitations.random_forest_training_provenance: Verified. The committed Random Forest artifact (rul_model.pkl) was trained on 80 engines using train_test_split(random_state=42), matching Cell 20/26 in the training notebook. The 20 evaluation engines are strictly held-out with zero cross-engine leakage.
audit_findings_and_limitations.isolation_forest_training_provenance_cav: Disclosed Limitation. In notebooks/Anamoly_Detection.ipynb (Cell 31), healthy_df was filtered from the entire 100-engine dataset (RUL > 100) before engine-level train/test separation. Therefore, nominal cycles from the 20 evaluation engines were present during Isolation Forest fitting, introducing cross-engine group leakage in the anomaly detector training phase.
audit_findings_and_limitations.lead_time_caveat: The previously claimed ~40-46 cycles lead time was an anecdotal single-engine observation (Engine 1 = 43 cycles). Across the full test fleet, first alert lead times vary widely due to a ~5.7% false alarm rate in nominal cycles. Requiring 3 consecutive anomaly flags yields a more reliable median lead time of 66.5 cycles.
audit_findings_and_limitations.ground_truth_limitation: NASA C-MAPSS FD001 is a continuous thermodynamic degradation simulation without discrete fault injection timestamps. Precision and recall are evaluated relative to operational regimes (nominal RUL > 100 vs degraded RUL <= 30 and RUL <= 50). A 100% degraded-regime recall reflects continuous abnormal sensor drift prior to functional breakdown, not flawless real-world discrete failure prediction.
